review_status: auto-reviewed: Claude checked every Spanish line (see docs/LANGUAGE_REVIEW.md); no native speaker, by the owner's decision
variety: Numbers and these price phrases are identical in Argentina and Mexico, so either female voice may read them. Argentine accent is welcome but not required.
pronunciation_note: English-style respelling, capitals mark the stressed syllable. Argentine accent: "ll" and "y" sound like "sh".

phrases.when: Two syllables. The v is soft, close to a b: NWEH-beh.
One syllable. Latin America says the z like an s: dyess, not dyeth.
Point at the thing and ask. In Argentina you will also hear “¿Cuánto sale?”.
Say it after you hear the price. Caro means expensive; the opposite is barato.

hook: Count to ten and ask a price in Spanish.

quiz.prompt: How do you ask the price?

outro: Say them out loud. Follow for the next topic.
